long_biography.plain_text:
Toni Fingerroos named his future games company at ten, while making a racing game on his grandmother’s computer. He thought games needed a company behind them and chose Fingersoft. The name survived unsuccessful ventures, including a studio that exhausted its funding before releasing a game and a sports-car business that consumed his savings.

For the eventual Hill Climb Racing breakthrough, he paired game design with a ready-made audience. His camera applications already produced advertising income that helped finance development, and he promoted the new game to their users. Later, he began publishing other studios’ work and invested in Phoenix Games, which helps smaller developers build their businesses.
